transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I keep making these small but embarrassing mistakes on things I’m submitting, like applications or research notes. I’ll think I checked it over, but then later I realize I skipped a question or put the wrong date on an artwork or something like that. It’s been frustrating enough that I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Have you noticed any feelings of anxiety or excessive worry that happen before or during these tasks where you make mistakes?

Not really, no. I mean, I get annoyed or embarrassed after I notice the mistake, but I don’t think I’m feeling especially anxious before or while I’m doing it. At least I haven’t noticed that being the main thing.

Have you been having any thoughts or impulses that keep coming up, even if you don’t want them, like needing to check something repeatedly or thinking something might happen if you don’t do something a certain way?

No, I don’t think so. I don’t really get stuck with thoughts like that, and I’m not checking things over and over because I feel like something bad will happen. It’s more like I miss stuff without realizing it.
Have you experienced any stressful or traumatic events recently or in the past that might be affecting your focus or attention?
I can’t think of anything like that, no. Nothing recent or from the past really comes to mind that feels connected to this.
Do you often find it hard to organize your tasks or keep your work space neat, even when you try to stay on top of it?

Yeah, that’s pretty common for me. My apartment and my laptop both kind of end up messy in the same way—rent papers, gallery notes, article PDFs, random to-do lists all over the place. I try to keep track of things, but then it turns into a bunch of half-started stuff, and I have trouble figuring out what actually needs to get done first.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, even when you’re trying to pay attention, like losing track of what you’re doing or getting easily distracted?

Yeah, that happens a lot. If I’m trying to read or write at my desk, it doesn’t take much to pull me off track—like a siren outside, someone talking in the hallway, or even just a random thought about an exhibit idea. Then suddenly I’ve been off doing or thinking about something else for twenty minutes before I realize I stopped.
When you think about having trouble staying focused or getting distracted, did you also experience that when you were younger, like in school or doing homework as a child?

Yeah, it did go back that far. In elementary school, teachers would say I had good ideas, but I’d forget to turn in worksheets or lose the instructions. I’d miss small details too, unless my parents checked my backpack every night.

Do you notice these issues with focus and organization in other areas of your life, like at home or in social situations, or do they mostly happen when you're working on tasks for your job or studies?

It’s not just work or school stuff. At home it shows up a lot too—my apartment gets covered in rent papers, notes, random to-do lists, that kind of thing. My laptop is the same way with PDFs and files everywhere. I’ll have a bunch of things started, and then I get stuck trying to figure out what actually needs to come first.
Do you also notice these kinds of focus or organization problems when you're in social situations, like hanging out with friends or at events?
I’m not totally sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed it as clearly with friends or at events. It’s more obvious to me when I’m trying to get something done or keep track of stuff.
